title: ASDLC example authored content
viewing_intent: A six-slide introduction on a laptop, desktop or shared screen; compose and inspect at 1280×720. Phone checks verify proportional scaling, not comfortable long-form reading.
authorship: Content and representations were selected and written from current ASDLC sources before composition. Kata is applied to this frozen copy and these slide boundaries.

slides.label: A FIELD GUIDE
slides.title: Agentic software development lifecycle
slides.notes: ASDLC stands for Agentic Software Development Lifecycle. This is an introduction to the site’s current framework and pattern library. Its recommendations are composable choices for a project, not a guarantee of deterministic model behaviour.
slides.content: A pattern library for building software with agents. People design and govern the system. Agents carry out the work.

slides.label: THE OPERATING MODEL
slides.title: Three layers of agentic work
slides.notes: The table retains the three layers, functions and human-role associations from Getting Started. These roles describe responsibilities, not necessarily three separate people. Humans remain responsible for designing the operating model.
slides.content: ASDLC’s three layers and the human role in each Layer Function Human role Context The supply chain—requirements, schemas, specs delivered just-in-time Editor Agents The logistics layer—moving information, generating code, running tests Operator Gates Quality control—deterministic checks + human oversight Governor

slides.label: DURABLE CONTEXT / BOUNDED WORK
slides.title: Keep the state. Name the change.
slides.notes: The current Spec pattern describes spec-anchored development, and rejects treating specs as the sole source from which all code is regenerated. The code block is an illustrative outline, not a complete template. A PBI defines the change and references permanent context; it does not copy the full design. Source: https://asdlc.io/patterns/the-pbi/
slides.content: The Spec STATE · LIVES WITH THE CODE The feature’s design and quality contract, kept current as the system changes. ## Blueprint Context, architecture, constraints ## Contract Done criteria, guardrails, scenarios Illustrative outline The PBI DELTA · CLOSED AFTER MERGE One scoped change, pointing to the spec and its verification criteria. A Product Backlog Item sets the task’s boundaries and how discoveries will be handled. When a change alters the contract, update the spec with it. Specs capture intent and constraints. Code remains authoritative for runtime logic.

slides.label: QUALITY, REVIEW AND ACCEPTANCE
slides.title: Different checks. Different questions.
slides.notes: This slide summarises output gates. The source also describes input gates for filtering and summarising context. Its three output tiers have different purposes; passing toolchain checks does not establish usability or strategic fit. The Context Gates pattern is Experimental as read on 17 October 2026.
slides.content: Quality DETERMINISTIC Does it compile and pass tests? Toolchain checks: types, lint, tests and build. Review PROBABILISTIC Does it satisfy the spec’s contracts? AI-assisted review of meaning, constraints and edge cases. Acceptance HUMAN JUDGMENT Is it the right thing? Usability, visual balance and strategic fit. ASDLC’s Context Gates pattern is marked Experimental.

slides.label: GETTING STARTED
slides.title: Try one bounded change
slides.notes: The sequence is explicitly supplied by the Getting Started page; it is not inferred from prose by Kata. A gate may send work back for correction, and discoveries can update the spec during implementation. This is an introductory loop, not a complete workflow for every team.
slides.content: Spec PBI Implementation Gate Merge The introductory loop from ASDLC’s Getting Started guide. Give the agent the relevant context and a clear outcome to work toward. Review the evidence before accepting the change. Keep the spec current as the work teaches you more.

slides.label: ASDLC.IO
slides.title: Build the system around the work.
slides.notes: The site describes optionality as a feature: patterns are composable choices. The guide links to concepts, patterns and practices for understanding the framework or applying one bounded change. Open the linked guide for the current material.
slides.content: Choose the patterns your project needs. Make the constraints and decisions explicit. Start with the guide ↗
